summary: A memo asking for reactions to a proposal to form an OS/2 user group. It is an informal request, not a protocol specification.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo asks whether individual OS/2 users would join a national user group. The Phoenix Group planned to collect responses and use them to decide whether to approach IBM about the proposal.

subtitle: A request for feedback on forming a national OS/2 user group.

tldr.problem: The Phoenix Group was assessing whether individual OS/2 users wanted a national group to communicate their views to IBM.
tldr.mechanism: The memo describes a straw poll and asks interested users to send their names and addresses to one of two email addresses.
tldr.outcome: The founders planned to compile responses and, if interest was strong, approach IBM management about a group.

today: RFC 1501 is Informational and records a proposal to gauge interest in a national OS/2 user group. It does not specify an IAB standard.

sections.title: Why Propose an OS/2 User Group
sections.content:
The Phoenix Group was considering whether there was a need for a national OS/2 users' group aimed at individual users. The memo says existing user organizations such as SHARE, GUIDE, COMMON, and DECIUS provided a way for members to communicate shared views to their hardware or software providers.

The authors say they saw no comparable representative voice for individual OS/2 users with IBM.
sections.plainLanguage: The Phoenix Group wanted to learn whether individual OS/2 users needed an organization to share their views with IBM. The memo compares this idea with other user groups.

sections.title: How the Group Measured Interest
sections.content:
The Phoenix Group was taking a straw poll across electronic forums to estimate the need for a user group and its potential membership. The memo lists a founding council of ten people and says that, if responses were strong, the group was prepared to approach IBM PSP senior management.

Interested readers were asked to send their name and address to either of two email addresses. The organizers said they would compile a database of responses and keep participants informed electronically.
sections.plainLanguage: Readers could email their contact details to show interest. The organizers planned to count responses before deciding whether to approach IBM.

sections.title: Status of the Memo
sections.content: RFC 1501 asks for reactions to the user-group proposal. It says it does not specify an IAB standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo is a request for feedback, not a technical standard.
